title: Language-specific SDK retry contracts and opt-in resumable streaming guides
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: SDK users across Python/TypeScript/Go are encountering ambiguous retry behavior and poor streaming ergonomics when networks or backends transiently fail. Current error surfaces differ between languages (exceptions vs error objects vs returned error tokens), and there is no clear opt-in path for resumable streaming or guidance on when to retry vs when to surface an actionable message to the application.

Goal: Define per-language retry contracts and a small opt-in resumable streaming API pattern with clear developer examples and migration notes. The deliverable should include API signatures, canonical error codes (string enums), human-friendly actionable messages, retry hint metadata, and idiomatic examples for Python, TS, and Go. We must avoid changing existing stable blocking APIs; this work should be additive and backwards-compatible where possible.

Scope:
- Standardize a minimal set of error codes and a short mapping table to HTTP and transport-level errors.
- Define a RetryHint metadata envelope that SDKs expose consistently (request_id, code, retryable, backoff_hint_ms, resume_token optional).
- Propose an opt-in resumable streaming SDK helper that persists/accepts resume_token and can continue from last committed message.
- Provide idiomatic examples and a migration guide for each language, and tests that simulate transient failures and resume flows.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: changing server-side protocol or enforcing resume semantics at runtime; large refactors of existing SDK exception hierarchies.

Why this matters: Reduces developer confusion, decreases app-layer bugs from naive retries, and improves UX for streaming-based features (chat, long outputs) under flaky networks.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical error code list (<= 12 codes) documented and published to the SDK repo README and central api-error-codes.md
SDKs (Python, TS, Go) expose RetryHint metadata in error objects or exceptions with identical field names and units
An opt-in resumable streaming helper implemented in each SDK that demonstrates resume via resume_token in integration tests
Examples for each language showing: (a) safe retry loop for idempotent requests, (b) client resume after transient stream failure, (c) how to surface actionable messages to end-users
Automated tests simulate network drop and validate resume_token correctness and backoff behavior under CI
Migration notes for existing customers and deprecation plan for any old, conflicting error shapes (if applicable)
tasks: Draft canonical error code list and mapping to HTTP/transport layers
Design RetryHint schema and field semantics (units and optionality)
Prototype Python exception wrapper that includes retry_hint and resume_token
Prototype TypeScript error class and helper types (preserve existing thrown shapes where possible)
Prototype Go error type with accessor methods for RetryHint fields
Implement opt-in streaming helper per language with small integration harness
Write per-language examples and migration guide (CONFLUENCE/Drive link)
Create unit + integration tests that simulate disconnects and verify resume behavior
Collect review feedback from SDK leads and Security for the hint exposure
Publish PRs, changelog notes, and announce in SDK channels
updates: 2026-02-11 - Kickoff: Scoped the work with SDK leads (Python: Nikhil Rao, TS: Clara Diaz, Go: Tomás Ortega). Agreed on additive approach and narrow RetryHint fields.

2026-02-18 - Drafted initial error code list and RetryHint proposal: non_exhaustive set: RATE_LIMIT, UNAVAILABLE, TIMEOUT, BAD_REQUEST, AUTH_FAILURE, INTERNAL, CANCELLED, RESUMABLE_EOF. Shared to #sdk-errors for feedback.

2026-02-23 - Implemented Python prototype: raises RedwoodError(Exception) with .retry_hint dict attached. Integration harness demonstrated resume_token resume in local test with simulated 100ms outage. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/412

2026-02-27 - TS and Go prototypes started. TS will use a typed Error subclass and optional ResumeController helper. Go will use an error wrapper type with accessor funcs to avoid breaking comparisons.

2026-03-03 - Design review notes: avoid embedding raw server stack traces in actionable messages; prefer short human strings and a link to debug docs. Security requested review of any tokens persisted to disk. Assigned follow-up to Ethan.
2026-03-05 - Implemented CI test harness that replays a recorded stream and injects network errors at deterministic offsets. Next: finish TS/Go tests and prepare cross-SDK examples.
